content: Public bodies spent £3.4bn on private consultants last year, with government spending up 62% since 2019-20 and still above pre-pandemic levels. The figures highlight the difficulty of Keir Starmer’s goal to cut consultancy spending in half, especially as large new contracts, including one with KPMG to train civil servants, continue to be awarded. Critics argue that heavy reliance on consultants is costly and often ineffective. Is there anything else I can help with?
